partners.diseaseBName: pyogenic bacterial infections due to MyD88 deficiency
partners.mechanism_chain: MYD88 (HGNC:7504) —DISRUPTS→ Toll-like receptor signaling pathway (GO:0007169); Toll-like receptor signaling pathway (GO:0007169) —LEADS_TO→ Pyogenic bacterial infections (HP:0002714); IRAK4 (HGNC:10988) —DISRUPTS→ Toll-like receptor signaling pathway (GO:0007169); Toll-like receptor signaling pathway (GO:0007169) —LEADS_TO→ Immunodeficiency (HP:0002705). partners.mechanism_chain: IRAK4 (HGNC:6072) —DISRUPTS→ NF-kappa B signaling (WP:WP413); NF-kappa B signaling (WP:WP413) —LEADS_TO→ Immunodeficiency (HP:0002705); PDGFRB (HGNC:9104) —DISRUPTS→ PDGFRB signaling pathway (WP:WP1006); PDGFRB signaling pathway (WP:WP1006) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal overgrowth (HP:0005094); PDGFRB signaling pathway (WP:WP1006) —LEADS_TO→ Craniofacial dysmorphism (HP:0000252); PDGFRB signaling pathway (WP:WP1006) —LEADS_TO→ White matter lesions (HP:0012747). Loss-of-function mutations in IRAK4 disrupt the NF-kappa B signaling pathway, leading to immunodeficiency (Disease A). Gain-of-function mutations in PDGFRB dysregulate the PDGFRB signaling pathway, causing skeletal overgrowth, craniofacial dysmorphism, and white matter lesions (Disease B). ### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. pyogenic bacterial infections due to MyD88 deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.477)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-1257604, Reactome:R-HSA-166058, Reactome:R-HSA-5603037, Reactome:R-HSA-5603041, Reactome:R-HSA-6811558)

**Proposed mechanism:** MYD88 (HGNC:7504) —DISRUPTS→ Toll-like receptor signaling pathway (GO:0007169); Toll-like receptor signaling pathway (GO:0007169) —LEADS_TO→ Pyogenic bacterial infections (HP:0002714); IRAK4 (HGNC:10988) —DISRUPTS→ Toll-like receptor signaling pathway (GO:0007169); Toll-like receptor signaling pathway (GO:0007169) —LEADS_TO→ Immunodeficiency (HP:0002705). Loss-of-function mutations in MYD88 (and IRAK4 for immunodeficiency 67) disrupt the Toll-like receptor signaling pathway, which is critical for innate immune responses against pyogenic bacteria. This disruption leads to recurrent pyogenic bacterial infections and a general state of immunodeficiency.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with MYD88 mutations who do not exhibit recurrent pyogenic bacterial infections or immunodeficiency, or demonstration that the Toll-like receptor signaling pathway is fully functional despite MYD88 deficiency in these patients. _(variant: Exome sequencing data from gnomAD showing a common pathogenic variant in MYD88 associated with these phenotypes.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of MYD88 in these conditions could lead to targeted therapeutic strategies aimed at boosting the Toll-like receptor signaling pathway or its downstream components to improve immune defense against bacterial pathogens in affected individuals.
